title: Seller's Property Disclosure Statement
description: Oregon requires sellers of residential real property to complete and deliver a Seller's Property Disclosure Statement to the buyer. The form covers title, water/sewer, structural, heating/cooling, environmental, and other known conditions. Must be delivered to the buyer within 5 business days after mutual acceptance of the offer unless delivered earlier. Buyer has 5 business days to revoke the offer after receiving the disclosure.

required_actions.note: Buyer has 5 business days to revoke offer after receiving disclosure. Exemptions include foreclosure, court-ordered transfers, and new construction.

title: Initial Agency Disclosure Pamphlet
description: Oregon requires real estate licensees to provide the Initial Agency Disclosure Pamphlet at the first contact with a prospective buyer or seller. Oregon recognizes seller's agents, buyer's agents, and disclosed limited agents (dual agency). Disclosed limited agency requires written informed consent of all parties.

title: Seismic / Earthquake Zone Disclosure
description: Oregon requires disclosure of seismic hazards affecting the property. Oregon sits within the Cascadia Subduction Zone, presenting significant earthquake risk. Sellers must disclose any known earthquake damage and whether the property is in a mapped seismic hazard zone. For commercial buildings, seismic retrofit disclosure may be required. The Oregon Resilience Plan identifies specific high-risk zones throughout the state.

required_actions.note: Earthquake/seismic section on OR-SPDS. Must disclose known damage and seismic zone location.
Buyer should review DOGAMI seismic hazard maps for the property location.

citations: ORS 455.447 (seismic retrofit requirements for certain buildings)

title: Closing Type — Escrow / Title Company
description: Oregon residential closings are conducted through escrow, handled by licensed escrow agents, title companies, or attorneys. Attorney involvement is not required. Oregon is an escrow-closing state where a neutral third party (escrow officer) manages the closing process, document recording, and fund disbursement.

required_actions.note: Licensed escrow company or title company conducts closing. Escrow must be handled by licensed escrow agent per ORS 696.505.

title: Forestland / Wildfire Hazard Disclosure
description: Oregon requires disclosure when property is located near or adjacent to forestland, subjecting it to wildfire risk and potential restrictions. Sellers must disclose proximity to forestland and any obligations under the Oregon Forest Practices Act. Properties in the wildland-urban interface may have additional defensible space requirements.

required_actions.note: Property may be subject to Oregon Forest Practices Act restrictions and defensible space requirements under SB 762 (2021).

citations: ORS 477.015 et seq. (Oregon Forest Practices Act)

title: Property Tax Disclosure (Measure 5 / Measure 50)
description: Oregon has a unique property tax system resulting from Ballot Measures 5 (1990) and 50 (1997). The assessed value may differ significantly from real market value. Sellers should disclose the current assessed value, real market value, and any special assessments. Buyers should be aware that property taxes may change upon reassessment after transfer depending on Measure 50 compression calculations.

required_actions.note: Include current assessed value vs. real market value on OR-SPDS.
Buyer should consult county assessor for estimated post-sale property tax obligations.
